one_month_reasoning: No Salesforce earnings fall in the window: Q3 FY27 results historically land in early December (Q2 was Aug 26, Q1 May 27) [1]. In-window items are second-order: final settlement of the $25B ASR (expected October; retires more shares, already known) [1], closing of the Contentful (~$1.5B) and Fin (~$3.6B) deals (in guidance) [3], the late-October FOMC and peer software prints (ServiceNow, Microsoft) that can move the group. The stock has pulled back from ~$268 intramonth high to $231 after a +55% three-month run [15][4], so there are opposing short-horizon forces (post-earnings drift and momentum vs reversal after a sharp rally) that I treat as roughly cancelling. I therefore centre on today's price (median ~$232) with a monthly log-sd of ~12%, a little below 47%/3.5 = 13.4% because no earnings jump is scheduled; CRM's own historical monthly sd is ~10-11% [4].

fair_value.method: Blend of 15x P/E on Sep-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS of ~$17.3 (=$260, 60%) and a 6.5% SBC-adjusted FCF yield on ~$16/share NTM owner FCF (=$246, 40%) gives ~$254 twelve months out.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 consensus x ~1.12: ~10-11% revenue growth path to $63B FY30 target plus lower share count after the $25B ASR; margin flat at ~34%.

Today ~14.4-14.5x forward; June-2026 trough ~10x ($146 on ~$15 EPS); Dec-2022 trough ~17-18x; peers WDAY ~11x, NOW ~24x; S&P software & services ~22x. A mature ~11% grower with AI-seat risk gets a modest premium to today, well below the 2019-24 25-35x range.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF ~$17.3B less SBC ~$4.5B = ~$12.8B on ~800M shares = ~$16/share at 6.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Gives FY27 FCF ~$15.0B; FY28-29 assumed to grow ~10%/yr to give Sep-2027 NTM ~ $17.3B.
FY27 GAAP-to-non-GAAP margin bridge shows SBC 9.0% of revenue; deducted as a real cost.
Q3 guide 827M reflects the 103M initial ASR delivery only; final settlement plus open-market buybacks take it to ~800M.
Between trough-level ~9% (June 2026) and ~4-5% for sector-average multiples; with ~$28B net debt (~$39.3B debt vs $11.4B cash [1]) plus ~$5B deal cash [3], a higher-than-sector yield is warranted.

bear.story: AI-seat compression fears return (as in H1 2026 when the stock fell ~41%) or a 2027 recession (Polymarket 35%, thin) hits IT budgets; organic reacceleration stalls, FY29 EPS ~ $15.5 and multiple reverts to ~10x, near the June 2026 trough.

base.story: cRPO ~13-14%, subscription growth ~11-12%, margins ~34%, buybacks shrink the count; forward multiple drifts to ~15x on ~$17.3 NTM EPS.

bull.story: Agentforce/Data 360 ARR (~$3.9B, +210%) drives organic reacceleration toward the $63B FY30 target; software sector re-rates and CRM gets ~19x on ~$17.5 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$160 CRM would be ~9-10x forward EPS, back near the June-2026 AI-panic low ($146). Getting there most likely means cRPO growth has fallen back or management has cut guidance, i.e. the organic reacceleration seen at Q2 (net new ACV growth ahead of total ACV) has failed, rather than ordinary 47%-vol noise.

reasoning: Facts: FY27 guide is revenue $46.1-46.4B (+11-12%), non-GAAP operating margin 34.3% and non-GAAP EPS $16.67-16.71, but that EPS includes ~$2.98 of H1 investment gains, so core is ~$13.7. FY28 consensus is ~$16.0, so at $231 the stock is on ~14.4x forward [1][6][7]. Base rates from 20 years of CRM monthly closes [4]: the unconditional 12m log-return mean is +16% with sd 33%, and the last 10 years are mean +10%, sd 29%, 5th/95th percentiles -38%/+60%. After 3-month gains above 20% (n=37) the 12m median was +16% and 70% ended positive. After rebounds from drawdowns deeper than 35% (small n=6, mostly 2009/2020/2023) forward returns were very large. Those samples come from CRM's hyper-growth era, so I shade them heavily toward a mature 11% grower. History of this setup: the 2022-23 derating and turnaround doubled the stock from $133 to $263 within 12 months [4]. The 2026 cycle has already done most of its rebound, from $146 to a $268 intramonth high, i.e. +55% from June 15 to September 15 [12][13][15]. Valuation: sector multiples have compressed from ~32x to ~22x [16], and CRM sits between WDAY (~11x) and NOW (~24x) [9][16]. My fair value is ~$254 (15x P/E on ~$17.3 NTM EPS and a 6.5% SBC-adjusted FCF yield), about 10% above spot. Macro: Polymarket gives ~35% for a US recession by end-2027 (2026-09-24, thin ~$9.6K volume [10][11]), which fattens the left tail. Distribution: I use a mixture of 80% lognormal (median $250, sd 0.32) and 20% stress lognormal (median $190, sd 0.50). That puts the median at ~$241, P(>=$231) at ~55% and P(>=$162) at ~86%. The scenario-weighted mean is ~$250. Research was focused, and I did not look up options or implied volatility.
